AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 5, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL
MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION.
TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING, ATTEND THE MEETING IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS,
SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING:
(669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685 DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK
ON AN ITEM. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON
THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING - 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION
  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a) –
  Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County Sheriff representative, and other related City
  officials.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Randy Bradley
  Apostolic Lighthouse Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Betsy Carranza
  Public Safety Cadet

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes.

  II.  City Council to proclaim October as Power of Pink/Breast Cancer Awareness Month in the City of
  Norwalk.

  III.  City Council to recognize Coach Operators Griselda Madrid and Margie Rangel for service to the
  community.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Quarterly Sheriff’s Department update.

  3.  State of the City update.

CONSENT CALENDAR
 Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  September 21, 2021. 825-04

  Report

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period August 22, 2021 –
  September 4, 2021, in the total amount of $927,916.40. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  September 16, 2021 – September 29, 2021, in the total amount of $2,663,172.73. 640

  Report

  5.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – SEPTEMBER 22, 2021 - No action is required unless the
  City Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on the item where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  6.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-59 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – ADMINISTRATION
  DEPARTMENT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-59, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN
  RECORDS IN THE ADMINISTRATION DEPARTMENT. 870-02

  Report

  7.  AMENDMENT NO. 2 – AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE ON-CALL BUILDING & SAFETY AND PLANNING
  CONSULTING SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 2 to the
  agreement with Infrastructure Engineers to provide on-call professional building and planning
  consultant services in an amount not to exceed $248,496; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the agreement and any additional amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 300

  Report

  8.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-60 – BUDGET AMENDMENT – ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME
  HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR PLANNING CONTRACT SERVICES AND APPROVE ADDITIONAL
  SERVICES FOR A PLANNING CONTRACT FOR PROJECT NO. 7859 – Staff recommends City
  Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-60, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO ADD LOW AND MODERATE INCOME HOUSING ASSET FUNDS FOR PLANNING
  CONTRACT SERVICES FOR THE CALIFORNIA YOUTH AUTHORITY PROPERTY PROJECT
  NO. 7859, in the amount of $338,784; and

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute a letter agreement through the existing agreement with
  CSG Consultants, Inc. for additional identified services and such other services reasonably
  necessary thereto as determined by the City Manager related to the California Youth Authority
  property, City Project No. 7859, not-to-exceed $500,000, provided there is funding in the budget,
  separate from the existing contract compensation, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  320/610/1005-04-7859

  Report
   9.  PROJECT NOS. 7228, 7229, & 7230 – RESOLUTION NO. 21-63 - BUDGET AMENDMENTS – HSIP
  CYCLE 6 PROJECTS - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-63, A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE PROPOSITION C
  FUNDS TO HIGHWAY SAFETY IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM CYCLE 6 – PROJECT NOS 7228, 7229
  & 7230. 610/1005-04-7228/7229/7230

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  10. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  11. Resolution No. 21-61 – RESOLUTION NO. 21-61 – SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2021/22 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN AND RESOLUTION NO. 21-62 – BUDGET AMENDMENT –
  REALLOCATE PRIOR YEAR UNUSED PROGRAM FUNDS TO THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT
  PROGRAM - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 21-61, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING A SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22
  ANNUAL ACTION PLAN; and

  b.  adopt Resolution No. 21-62, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT FUNDS TO THE
  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM, in the amount of $1,100,000. 315/610

  Report

ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  12. ORDINANCE NO. 21-1728 AMENDING THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE BY ENACTING A NEW
  CHAPTER 8.50 “ORGANIC WASTE DISPOSAL REDUCTION” – Staff recommends City Council
  introduce by title only Ordinance No. 21-1728, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL AMENDING
  THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE BY ENACTING A NEW CHAPTER 8.50 “ORGANIC WASTE
  DISPOSAL REDUCTION, and schedule for second reading.

  Report

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 21-64 - AUTHORIZING THE CITY TO CONTINUE TO TELECONFERENCE OPEN
  MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361 - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution
  No. 21-64, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING
  THE CITY TO CONTINUE TO TELECONFERENCE OPEN MEETINGS PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY
  BILL 361.

  Report

REPORTS

  14. 6TH CYCLE HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE – STATUS UPDATE - Staff recommends City Council
  receive and file this report. 320-02-03

  Report

  15. AWARD OF CONTRACT – ONLINE PERMITTING AND LICENSING SOFTWARE - Staff recommends
  City Council:

  a.  approve an agreement with EdgeSoft, Inc. for an online permitting and licensing software program
  effective November 1, 2021 through November 30, 2026 in an amount not to exceed $340,140 for
   the first year’s software licenses, training, implementation and data migration, including integration
  to existing programs; the remaining years will not exceed $80,000 annually plus 5% each year for
  software maintenance and data hosting;

  b.  approve an electronic plan review system, with a company to be determined, to integrate with the
  new software in an amount not to exceed $50,000 for the first year of implementation and training;
  the remaining years will not exceed $25,000 annually plus 5% each year; and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute all agreements and any amendments provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 634-04

  Report

  16. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – OCTOBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated September 30, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
